_meta.description: Spitfire Abbey Road Orchestra Percussion — the instrument CATALOG for this piece's percussionist (one lane, P4): for each instrument, the MIDI key → beater / articulation map of its All-in-One preset. This file says what the library offers; which instruments the piece USES is bank/perc_selection.json, and tools/apply_perc.js turns that selection into the percussion techniques in sandbox/instruments.js (the ARO_PERC block).
_meta.source: piece #2 (composition_for_two_pianos_and_two_percussion) docs/instrument_map.json, lastUpdated 2026-04-05 — carried 2026-09-17 with piece #2's rack routing (its Perc1-A/B/C ports, channels, sourceCh) and its four piano entries stripped; every other field verbatim. Re-carry the same way if piece #2 maps more instruments.
_meta.octaveConvention: Spitfire default: C3 = MIDI 60 (middle C). Reaper matches Spitfire numbering. The `note` names in this file are Spitfire's; the `midi` numbers are absolute (middle C = 60) and are the only thing the recipe reads.
_meta.status: verified = dictated key by key from the lit keys of the plugin's keyboard · partial / predicted = some keys inferred, spot-check before use · skeleton = name and beaters from the manual only, NO keys — map it (walkthrough) before it can be selected.
_meta.walkthrough: To map an instrument: load its All-in-One preset in the Spitfire plugin, hover over each lit key from the lowest up, dictate note name + label (e.g. "C2, Poly Beater Low Hit L"); the AI writes the entry's allInOne. Piece #2's PROJECT_JOURNAL §5.1 is the full procedure.
_meta.lgmfAdditions: 2026-09-18 (piece #6): Finger Cymbals and Bell Tree mapped from the composer's hover of the Small Metals (C) preset — the first entries NOT carried from piece #2. Note they were mapped inside the FAMILY preset, not an All-in-One, and that TWO-HANDED LAYOUT is on in his instance, so each pattern repeats +24 (`duplicateOf`). RUNNING_LOG §41.

patternRules.description: Observed mapping rules across verified instruments
rules: Natural keys (C,D,E,F,G,A) = primary articulations: Hit L, Hit R, Roll
Black keys (sharps) = variants: rim hits (single-pitch) or pitch variants (multi-pitched)
C-E block = first beater/technique group per octave half
F-A block = second beater/technique group per octave half
Each octave in All-in-One = one pitch level (Low=oct2, High=oct3 for 2-pitch instruments)
Beaters without rim/roll skip those slots (e.g. Hand has Hit L + Hit R only, no roll)
Hit L = root note, Hit R = root + whole tone, Roll = root + major 3rd

bongos._notes: C2 group: Low Hands (C/D/E whole-tone) + Low Fingers (F, G, A whole-tone). C3 group: High Hands+Fingers (consecutive semitones C3-A3, includes closed variants). C4 group: Low Sticks (C/D/E whole-tone + F consecutive, G jump). C5 group: High Sticks (same pattern as C4).

log_drums._notes: Six log drums (1=highest, 6=lowest). Each drum has Left and Right hits. Four groups of 4 notes: Drums 6+5 at C-D#, Drums 4+3 at F-G#, Drums 2+1 at C(next oct)-D#. Groups repeat at oct2-3 and oct4-5 as variant pairs.

toys_claves.name: Claves
toys_claves.description: 3 clave pairs, each with Low and High pitch. Part of Toys preset.
toys_claves._notes: 3 clave pairs (3=lowest, 1=highest), each with Low/High hit. C-A whole-tone spacing per group. Two variant groups at oct2 and oct4. No beater distinction. Does NOT follow standard L/R pattern — each note is a distinct pitch.

toys_castanets.name: Castanets
toys_castanets.description: Machine + handle pair. Part of Toys preset. Two blocks per type (likely same samples mapped for performance convenience).

toys_whips.name: Whips

toys_guiros.name: Guiros

toys_caxixi.name: Caxixi

toys_maracas.name: Maracas
toys_maracas.description: Pair of maracas. Part of Toys preset. Two pitch levels (Low/High), each with Throw, Shakes, Swirls articulations. Two variant groups per pitch.
toys_maracas._notes: Four groups of 4 (Low oct2, High oct3, Low oct4, High oct5). Each group: Throw/Throw/Shakes/Swirls. Groups 1-2 and 3-4 are variant pairs for the same articulations.

bass_drum_alt.name: Bass Drum (Alt)
bass_drum_alt.description: Vintage 32-inch shallow open shell bass drum with defined attack and woody overtones.
bass_drum_alt._notes: Sticks group: chromatic C2-E2 (5 primary articulations), then naturals only F2-A2 for rim variants (Rim Hit L, Rim Hit R, Rim Roll — F#2 and G#2 gaps). Hard Felt groups (C3-A3) are whole-tone naturals only: C/D/E for Hard Felt, F/G/A for Hard Felt (Cloth Damped). Medium Felt, Rods, and Brushes (hits) groups are fully chromatic. Brushes sweeps (C6-E6) chromatic. Last assignment is E6 Swirling.

giant_taiko.name: Giant Taiko

toms_low.name: Toms Low

toms_low._notes: Two drum sizes: 14" (C2+C3 groups) and 13" (C4+C5 groups). Each size has two groups: Seq1 (sticks damped/open/rim) at C, Seq2 (felt/rods/brushes) at C+octave. C/D/E are whole-tone spaced (damped hit L/R + roll or felt hit L/R + roll), then F-A# consecutive semitones.

toms_high.name: Toms High
toms_high.description: Vintage silver single-headed toms, clear and resonant. All in One (High) preset. 12-inch and 10-inch drums. Sticks (damped, open, rim), Felt, Rods, Brushes.
toms_high._notes: Two drum sizes: 12" (C2+C3 groups) and 10" (C4+C5 groups). Same mapping pattern as toms_low. Each size has two groups: Seq1 (sticks damped/open/rim) at C, Seq2 (felt/rods/brushes) at C+octave. C/D/E are whole-tone spaced, then F-A# consecutive semitones.

crashes_and_stack.name: Crashes and Stack

giant_crasher.name: Giant Crasher

spiral_cymbal.name: Spiral Cymbal

small_metals_bell_tree.name: Bell Tree
small_metals_bell_tree.description: A cascade of small tuned bars swept with a mallet or finger — a shimmering gliss. Part of Small Metals.
small_metals_bell_tree._notes: Mapped 2026-09-18 from the composer's hover of the Small Metals (C) preset, dictated in order from the low C (RUNNING_LOG §41): six glisses on consecutive WHITE keys C-D-E-F-G-A, no black keys ('I dont think this uses the black keys'), repeated +24 ('the pattern starting on the c 2 octaves up is the same'). A meter sweep could NOT confirm it — the glisses ring far longer than the gap, so every key read the same tail; the state's rr_neighbourMax=45 for this articulation matches the sixth white key exactly, which does corroborate. Whether the +24 copy is the same samples is unsettled, his words: 'will figure this out another day'. The description was corrected here too: piece #2's skeleton called it 'cup-shaped bells played with poly mallets', which is the Temple Bowls, not a bell tree.

small_metals_mark_tree.name: Mark Tree
small_metals_mark_tree.description: Suspended metal tines producing signature glissandi. Part of Small Metals.

small_metals_agogos.name: Agogos
small_metals_agogos.description: Cone-shaped bell pairs in two regional styles (African, Latin American), each with Low and High pitch, Open and Closed hits. Part of Small Metals.
small_metals_agogos._notes: Two regional styles as 'beaters': African (oct2, oct4) and Latin American (oct3, oct5). Each style has Low (C-D# group) and High (F-G# group) pitch. Open/Closed on natural/sharp pairs, L/R on C-C#/D-D# pairs. Oct2-3 and oct4-5 are variant groups.

small_metals_spring_coil.name: Spring Coil
small_metals_spring_coil.description: Large coiled spring played with triangle beater — suspended (open) or resting (muted). Hits and rakes (fast/slow). Part of Small Metals.
small_metals_spring_coil._notes: No beater distinction. C-D# = Open/Muted Hit (L/R pairs). F-G# = Open/Muted Rake (Fast/Slow — 4 distinct articulations, no L/R). Two variant groups at oct2 and oct4.

small_metals_cowbells.name: Cowbells
small_metals_cowbells.description: Clapperless bells in 3 pitches struck with drum sticks. Part of Small Metals.

small_metals_cabassa.name: Cabassa
small_metals_cabassa.description: Beads wrapped around ridged metal cylinder, turned with handle. Rotation, handle flick, finger tap, palm hit, finger slap techniques. Part of Small Metals.
small_metals_cabassa._notes: No beater distinction. C-D# = Rotation/Handle Flick pairs (L/R), F-G = Finger Tap (L/R), C(next oct)-D# = Palm Hit/Finger Slap pairs (L/R). Two variant groups at oct2-3 and oct4-5.

small_metals_chain_drops.name: Chain Drops
small_metals_chain_drops.description: Heavy gauge chains dropped into trash can for aggressive metallic accents. Part of Small Metals.
small_metals_chain_drops._notes: Two groups (C2-G2, C4-G4) with same pattern: Drop/Drop/Swirls/Lift/Lift. No beater distinction. Gap between G2 and C4.

small_metals_finger_cymbals.name: Finger Cymbals
small_metals_finger_cymbals.description: Small cymbal pairs struck together for long high-pitched ring. Part of Small Metals.
small_metals_finger_cymbals._notes: Mapped 2026-09-18 from the composer's hover of the Small Metals (C) preset (RUNNING_LOG §41) and CONFIRMED by a meter sweep of ch 1: 36, 38, 60, 62 sound (≈ -29 dB); 40, 48, 50 silent (-154 dB). Two keys, Low and High, repeated +24 (TWO-HANDED LAYOUT is on in his instance). Whether the +24 copy is the same samples or a second set is unsettled — his words: 'not sure if this is just duplicate for performance or different samples will figure this out another day'.

small_metals_guira.name: Güira
small_metals_guira.description: Caribbean textured metal surface, tapped or scraped for rhythms. Part of Small Metals.

small_metals_reco_reco.name: Reco-Reco
small_metals_reco_reco.description: Springs across hollow metal frame, struck or scraped. Part of Small Metals.

small_metals_sleigh_bells.name: Sleigh Bells & Indian Bells
small_metals_sleigh_bells.description: Pellet bells on handle (sleigh) or rope (Indian), shaken for crisp jingle. Single Shake L/R and Long Shake/Roll. Part of Small Metals.
small_metals_sleigh_bells._notes: Two bell types as 'beaters': Sleigh Bells (oct2, oct4) and Indian Rope Bells (oct3, oct5). C/D/E whole-tone = Single Shake L / Single Shake R / Long Shake/Roll. Oct2-3 and oct4-5 are variant groups.

small_metals_tambourines.name: Tambourines
small_metals_tambourines.description: Set of 3 tambourines (Pop, Alt, Orchestral), shaken or hand-struck. Part of Small Metals.
small_metals_tambourines._notes: 3 tambourine types as 'beaters'. C2-G4 = layer 1, C5-G7 = layer 2 (same articulations, likely round robin). Spitfire labels Short Shake and Accent identically on both C/D and C#/D# — disambiguated here as L/R. Alt Tambourine uses open/closed hand techniques with L/R already in Spitfire labels. Orchestral has no Hand Roll (7 keys vs Pop's 8).

small_metals_wind_chimes.name: Wind Chimes
small_metals_wind_chimes.description: Small suspended metal tines adding light splashes of colour. Part of Small Metals.

small_metals_triangles.name: Small Metals Triangles
small_metals_triangles.description: Triangle set with Low, Middle, and High pitch levels. Hit, Choked Hit, Roll, and three Damped durations per pitch. C5–C7 duplicate Low with separate samples.

suspended_cymbals.name: Suspended Cymbals
suspended_cymbals.description: Set of 3: 20-inch Dark, 21-inch Mellow, 16-inch Bright. Huge range of crashes and shimmering textures. Has bows/scrapes.
suspended_cymbals._note: Has separate All in One presets per cymbal: Dark, Mellow, Bright

temple_bowls.name: Temple Bowls
temple_bowls.description: Set of 4 temple bowls with rich blooming sustain. Multi-pitched.
temple_bowls._notes: Four groups of 4 entries. Each octave has a low pair (Bowls 4&3, starting at C) and a high pair (Bowls 2&1, starting at F), chromatic within each pair. Rubber Mallet in octave 2, Brush in octave 3. E and A positions (E2, E3, A2, A3) are unused within each beater group.

thundersheet.name: Thundersheet
thundersheet.description: Extremely large (64x42 inch) thin suspended metal sheet. Has bows and superball FX.

trash_cans.name: Trash Cans
trash_cans.description: Spread pair of trash cans for street sound, layering, and complex polyrhythms.

waterphone.name: Waterphone
waterphone.description: Metal tines around water-filled chamber, bowed for otherworldly sounds with mesmerising harmonics.

wind_gong.name: Wind Gong
wind_gong.description: 26-inch wind gong with quick bright attack producing rushing-wind sound.
